scope: SlotBindings metadata reuse/refill and grouped private slot controls; CPU/CUDA component contracts only.
outcome: Image 1 ran CPU20 and CUDA9: 26 passed, three new batch fixtures failed before their intended execution. Only those three fixtures were rebuilt and retried on image 2; all passed. Image 2 did not rerun the other 26 cases.
implementation: SlotBindings::clear releases old lease/address facts while retaining prepared metadata and counts; refill checks all original domain/generation/extent facts before consuming any caller writer.

Common Store controls group by actual resource, ExecutionSource and original Queue identity; one fixed I32 carrier holds disjoint per-Store source/destination slices and uploads once per original group.

Batch bind validates a complete cohort, duplicate owners and real permissions before moving transactions. A late read-projection failure withdraws earlier installed permissions and returns all original caller transactions.
A partial take cannot overwrite a shared carrier while another transaction remains. Real result/completion retirement and reset revocation retain the original guards and owner-return contracts.
The two resource reservation callers now pass only their new required reads; reserve_reads itself already includes the existing bindings.

checked_contracts.refill: Two new GraphSlots cases verify unchanged metadata addresses and no new attempts from the rejecting metadata allocator, old read guards released, live-writer/count/foreign-domain rejection and unchanged caller ownership.
checked_contracts.accounting: The retained metadata-failure case checks failed-allocation cleanup, metadata-only ResourceBudget charges, unchanged payload pool allocation, clear retaining its metadata charge, and full refund when the transaction owner is destroyed.
checked_contracts.batch_cpu: Two new cases check same carrier/different slice offsets over two rounds, changed slot order via refill, partial/duplicate cohort rejection, partial-take gating, reset recovery and a deliberately late real permission failure with successful retry after removing only the blocker.
checked_contracts.batch_cuda: The new double-Store case runs two rounds on the original CUDA Queue, verifies one device carrier with fixed disjoint offsets and changed IDs, checks copied values and untouched sentinel slots; partial bind leaves caller owners intact.
checked_contracts.retained_cuda_regressions: The original indexed GDN3 and conv4 cases all passed on image 1 after the product changes, including the conv F32 two RequireCapture submissions with record1/reuse0 then changed-destination record0/reuse1, BF16 long chunk, F16 raw history bits, and legal escaping-Gather fallback.

boundaries: No claim that the whole bind/submit path performs zero allocations: only the explicit refill metadata allocator contract and fixed carrier identities were tested.

The Apple/Vulkan original-native ExecutionSource upload branch was not run in this batch. Its temporary helper metadata uses the selected/budget allocator; queried native payload scratch is separately reserved and refunded on success, retained on possibly accepted failure. This is source-reviewed accounting, not native-fault injection or a measured no-allocation claim.
CPU direct-host and common CUDA Queue controls executed. CUDA Store/GDN/conv kernels did execute; zero NVCC means no native recompilation, not absence of GPU execution.
No real GPU fault, unknown-retirement fault injection, full model/engine run, MTP quality assessment, tokens/s measurement, memory performance comparison or speedup conclusion.
GTest/process durations are preserved for provenance and are not performance benchmarks.
The complete final image did not rerun all 29 cases: final status combines 26 prior passes with three successful fixture-only retries.

failures.observed: Unqualified single-request wrapper bind with std::array participated in std::bind overload resolution; C2440.
failures.correction: Qualify the existing slots::bind overload and pass an explicit span. The same final source also clears borrowed scratch references on every return without allocation.

failures.observed: Three new batch fixtures threw Bad expected access.
failures.diagnosis: Source inspection located the unchecked GraphBuilder.finish result: two unknown external Store effects lacked the required explicit ordering edge.
failures.correction: Only CPU/CUDA test fixtures add Store1 depends_on Store0 and clearer Result status diagnostics. Product objects are identical between the two executed images.

provenance.hardware: Actual CUDA stderr reports NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070, capability 8.9, 12281 MiB; full toolchain/device identities are referenced from the unchanged indexed-conv baseline receipt, not freshly queried here.
